blocks.text: His majesty is above earth and heavens. When He raises the condition of His people, then there is glory to all His pious ones, the Children of Israel, the people near Him, Halleluyah.

blocks.text: Psalm of David: Ascribe to the Lord, sons of the powerful, ascribe to the Lord honour and might. Ascribe to the Lord the honour of His Name, bow down before the Lord in holy array. The voice of the Lord is above the waters, the God of glory has thundered, the Lord is above mighty waters. The voice of the Lord is power, the voice of the Lord is beauty. The voice of the Lord shatters cedars, the Lord shattered cedars of Lebanon. He made them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like young unicorns. The voice of the Lord makes the wilderness tremble, the Lord makes the wilderness of Kadesh tremble. The voice of the Lord causes hinds to calve, and strips forests and in His sanctuary everything expresses honour. The Lord was enthroned as King for eternity. The Lord gives strength to His people, the Lord blesses His people with peace.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'sanctu-ary' across a line break; I joined it as 'sanctuary'. A faint speck after 'cedars,' looks like an artifact. 'eternity.' looks slightly smudged.
This is the heading of the right column.

blocks.text: By David, a psalm. The earth belongs to the Lord together with the fullness of it, the world and those who dwell in it. For He has founded it above the seas and established it over rivers. Who may ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who remain in His holy place? The clean of hands and the pure of heart, who has not taken my soul for vanity nor sworn falsely. He will receive blessing from the Lord and kindness from the God of his salvation. This is the generation of those that seek Him, that desire Thy countenance, Jacob, Selah. Lift up your heads, O gates, and lift yourselves up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of Glory may enter. Who is this King of Glory? He is the Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in war. Lift up your heads, O gates, lift up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of Glory may come. Who is this King of Glory? The Lord of Hosts, He is the King of Glory, Selah.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'gen-eration' across a line break; I joined it. In the first 'Who is this King of Glory?' the word 'of' looks like 'ot' in the scan; I read it as 'of'. The source capitalisation 'Thy' and lower-case 'his salvation' are kept as printed.

blocks.text: When the scroll of the Torah is returned to the Holy Ark:

uncertainties: No vowel points are visible on this word.

blocks.text: When it rested He said: ‘Return, O Lord, to the myriads of thousands of Israel’. Arise, O Lord, to Thy resting-place, Thou and the Ark of Thy strength. Thy priests are clothed in righteousness and Thy pious ones exult. For the sake of David, Thy servant, do not turn back the face of Thine anointed. For a fine portion have I given you, do not forsake my Torah. It is a tree of life for those who grasp it and whoever supports it is made happy. Its ways are delightful ways and all its paths are peace. Restore us, O Lord, to Thee, that we may return, renew our days as of old.
uncertainties: The page prints no scripture references here; the references are my own identification. 'resting-place' breaks across a line at the hyphen; I kept it as a real hyphenated compound. The source hyphenates 'delight-ful' across a line break; I joined it.

notes: Only one page was assigned (scan s197, printed page 88), although the instructions mention two pages. I read the full image and all four enlarged bands; where the bands overlap, I transcribed the text only once.

Most of the page is English. The only Hebrew is three unpointed linkage words: יהללו, הודו and ובנחה. There is no other Hebrew text, no cantillation, no pointing, no sound sequences, no Hebrew-script German and no footnotes.

The middle of the page has two parallel columns separated by a vertical rule. The left column, headed 'On the Sabbath:', has Psalm 29. The right column, headed 'On weekdays:', has Psalm 24. The two parenthetical psalm citations are printed inline in the text; I split them out as separate citation blocks.
Below the final line there is a short centred horizontal rule, and the rest of the page is blank. There is no bottom text.
